title: The Return Trip
transcript: A mail order clothing shop wanted to find out whether a reusable shipping envelope would lower its environmental impact. The new envelope required more material to make than the shop's usual paper mailer, so the shop tracked how many orders each one carried. During the first trial, customers could take empty envelopes to a collection point downtown, but many lived far from it. With so few envelopes coming back, the shop estimated that the reusable design had a higher impact per order. It then offered customers the option of handing back an empty envelope when a driver was already delivering their next order. Returns rose, and the estimated impact fell below that of the paper mailer on this route. The shop is now studying routes with fewer repeat customers.

questions.prompt: Why did the shop track how many orders each reusable envelope carried?
options: The envelope could hold only one item at a time.
Drivers charged the shop for each envelope they collected.
The envelope took more material to make than the usual mailer.
Customers were charged according to the number of times it was used.
questions.answer: The envelope took more material to make than the usual mailer.
questions.explanation: 可重复使用的信封耗材更多，店家因此追踪每个信封能分摊到多少笔订单。

questions.prompt: Why might the environmental result differ on routes with fewer repeat customers?
options: There may be fewer opportunities to collect envelopes during deliveries.
Paper mailers may carry more clothing on those routes.
Customers may receive their first orders more slowly.
Drivers may have less room to carry new envelopes.
questions.answer: There may be fewer opportunities to collect envelopes during deliveries.
questions.explanation: 回头客较少时，司机借下一次送货回收空信封的机会也可能减少。
